messages:
matt: Quick question about FP8/INT4 dequant fusion — do we plan to expose fusion knobs in the kernel API or keep them internal to the runtime?

rachel: short version: runtime should own selection, but kernel needs a clear contract (inputs, scratch, semantics).

aj: Agree. Kernel contract should accept quant metadata (format, scales, zero points, per-channel flag) and a boolean `fuse_dequant`. Kernels can implement fused path or fallback to dequant+compute.

sam: Main concern: KV cache. If we dequant Q/K into float for compute and also cache dequanted values, memory spikes. We should avoid duplicating buffers per-request. Prefer lazy dequant + shared per-GPU buffer pool.

priya: Also FP8 formats differ (E4M3 vs E5M2). Need a QFormat enum in the metadata so kernels know exponent/mantissa layout + implicit bias. Some calibrations will be very format-specific.

maria: For INT4 we probably need packed layout support in the kernel (nibbles). API should accept a `layout` hint (`packed`, `channel_major`, `row_packed`) so kernel can choose load/store.

matt: Can someone sketch the minimal C API we want? Keep it tiny — runtime picks variant and sets flags.

aj: Sketch: 
```
// quant metadata describes layout and scales
struct QuantMeta {
  enum QFormat {FP8_E4M3, FP8_E5M2, INT8_SYMM, INT8_ASYM, INT4_PPACKED};
  QFormat format;
  float* scales; // either single or per-channel (channels indicated elsewhere)
  int8_t* zeros; // optional for asymmetric
  int channels;
  bool per_channel;
};

int fused_attn_qk_dequant(const QuantMeta* Q_meta, const void* Q_data,
                         const QuantMeta* K_meta, const void* K_data,
                         const QuantMeta* V_meta, const void* V_data,
                         float* out, // float32 or fp16 output depending on opts
                         void* scratch, size_t scratch_bytes,
                         uint32_t opts_flags);
```

rachel: Nice. Add an `alloc_scratch` callback pointer in KernelOptions so runtime can control pooling/numa/streams.

sam: +1. Also `opts_flags` should include `KEEP_DEQUANTED_FOR_CACHE` so runtime can pick whether kernel writes dequanted KV into a provided cache pointer. That handles the cache-memory tradeoff explicitly.

perf-bot: perf-bot: quick microbenchmark (A100, seq=512, bs=8): fused_fp8_attn (fused dequant path) = 72ms, fp16_fallback = 98ms. INT4 packed fused = 65ms but with -0.6 ppl on eval set.

priya: Good to see numbers. We need a configurable accuracy/perf knob — default to fused for latency-sensitive routes, fallback to fp16 for strict accuracy routes.

maria: Calibration note: INT4 likely needs per-channel scales on weight matrices to avoid big accuracy loss. That means `scales` pointer will often be non-null and length=channels. Kernels must support per-channel broadcasting in the inner loop.

matt: Decision proposal: 
- Runtime picks kernel variant based on model metadata + heuristics (seq dist, batch, route tier).
- Kernel API is minimal and accepts quant metadata + `fuse_dequant` + `scratch` + `cache_ptr` optional.
- Kernels may implement fused dequant paths; runtime can set `KEEP_DEQUANTED_FOR_CACHE` if it wants kernel to write dequanted KV into cache region.
- Fall back to fp16/float kernels if quant kernel unavailable or accuracy gate triggered.

aj: Implementation followups: add unit tests for each QFormat, microbench harness that exercises cache/no-cache flows, and an integration test with the eval suite to detect regressions.

sam: Ops-level refactor: split attention into two kernel categories — `quant-aware` (expects quant inputs) and `quant-agnostic` (expects floats). Keeps selection simple.

priya: Edge cases: mixed precision per-layer (QKV int8, FFN fp16) — ensure model metadata allows per-layer precision tags and runtime respects them.

matt: Also need telemetry: per-request metric on which kernel chosen (+ accuracy regressions flagged by Optimize).

maria: Security: encrypted private deployments — quant metadata must not leak any data, but scales/zeros are fine as they are model-specific. Still mark as sensitive in audits.

rachel: Rollout plan: canary on Dedicated with `fuse_dequant=true` feature flag, monitor perf/accuracy. If good, enable on hosted routes with auto-fallback to `fp16` based on quality threshold.

matt: OK. Next tasks: aj to produce kernel API PR, sam to prototype shared scratch pool, priya to run calibration experiments comparing per-tensor vs per-channel INT4, maria to add telemetry + audit tags. We'll sync next week.

aj: I'll draft the API RFC and include microbench numbers and memory model notes.

matt: thanks all :thumbsup:
